page.title: AI Workflow Consulting Process Guide
page.description: Learn the steps, tools, and decisions to run an AI workflow consulting engagement from assessment to roadmap.
page.h1: How should an AI workflow consulting process be run?
page.definition: AI workflow consulting process is a structured engagement that assesses current operations, identifies high-value automation opportunities, selects appropriate tools, and delivers a prioritized roadmap with human-in-the-loop governance for marketing, content, and event teams.
page.quick_answer: Start with a current-state audit, map use cases by impact and effort, choose tools that fit your existing stack, and build a phased roadmap with named approvers for every AI output. West Peek Productions sets up human-in-the-loop AI workflows for marketing, content and event teams, scoped per engagement; send the scope for a quote.

sections.h2: What does an AI workflow assessment cover?

blocks.p: The assessment maps current processes, identifies manual handoffs, and scores each step for automation readiness.

ul: Inventory of recurring content, event, and marketing tasks with owners and tools
Measurement of cycle time, revision rounds, and approval bottlenecks
Classification of steps as deterministic, generative, or judgment-based
Risk rating for brand voice, compliance, and data privacy per workflow
Gap analysis between current stack and required AI capabilities

sections.h2: How do you prioritize use cases for automation?

blocks.p: Rank use cases by business impact, implementation effort, and risk tolerance to build a phased roadmap.

ul: Score each candidate on revenue influence, time savings, and error reduction
Estimate integration complexity with existing platforms and data sources
Flag workflows requiring legal review or executive sign-off
Group quick wins for pilot phase, strategic builds for second phase
Define success metrics per use case before development starts

sections.h2: Which tools fit a human-in-the-loop workflow?

blocks.p: Choose workflow orchestration, content generation, asset creation, and integration layers that support named approvers at every gate.

sections.h2: What does a consultant deliver versus an agency?

blocks.p: Consultants provide assessment, use-case list, tool choice, and roadmap; agencies build working automations, integrations, and documentation with ongoing support.

ul: Consultant output: an assessment, a prioritised use-case list, a tool choice and a roadmap
Agency output: working automations, integrations and documentation, often with a support retainer
Pricing models: day rate or fixed project for consultants; fixed build fee plus a monthly retainer for agencies
West Peek Productions sets up human-in-the-loop AI workflows for marketing, content and event teams; it is not a general AI consultancy

sections.h2: How do you govern AI outputs after launch?

blocks.p: Establish human-in-the-loop approval gates, monthly review cycles, and metrics for cycle time, revision rounds, and on-time rate.

ul: Human-in-the-loop rule: AI output is a draft until a named person approves it
Six components reviewed monthly: scope, tools, owners, metrics, risk, budget
Core metrics: cycle time, revision rounds, on-time rate and capacity use
Escalation path for brand voice deviations or compliance flags
Quarterly roadmap refresh based on performance data and new model capabilities

faq.q: How long does a typical AI workflow consulting engagement take?
faq.a: A first plan runs 90 days: long enough to see a trend, short enough to change course. Assessment and roadmap delivery usually complete in four to six weeks, followed by pilot implementation and monthly reviews.

faq.q: What internal roles must be assigned before starting?
faq.a: You need a workflow owner who signs off on automation scope, a brand approver for generated content, a technical lead for integration access, and a compliance contact for data and privacy review. Each gate requires a named person.

faq.q: Can we keep our current project management and publishing tools?
faq.a: Yes. The engagement maps your existing stack — Asana, Monday.com, HubSpot, WordPress, Webflow — and selects AI layers that connect through Zapier or Make without replacing core systems.

faq.q: What happens if the AI output fails quality checks?
faq.a: The human-in-the-loop rule treats every AI result as a draft. Failed outputs route back to the named approver with annotated feedback. The workflow pauses until the approver revises or rejects, preventing unpublished errors from reaching audiences.
